proofs.proof_tex:
First consider the generic pair in \(\texttt{def:outside-face-pair}\). Conditional on either cohort, both allocations have the four-wave observed law
\[
 (1-\varepsilon)P^\circ(X_{0:3}\in\cdot\mid D=d)
 +\varepsilon\delta_{(e,e,e,e)}.                           \tag{1}
\]
It is independent of whether the added atom receives label \(h\) or \(k\). The base law has no date-\(1\) absorbers. Since absorption implies \(X_0=e\Rightarrow X_1=e\), the base also has no mass at \(X_0=e\). Conditional on \((D,Z)\), the retained and added components are therefore separated by the current state until absorption: at an active current state the transition is the retained kernel, whereas at \(e\) the next state is deterministically \(e\). Thus each marginal potential path remains first-order Markov. Consistency, no anticipation, the two common untreated kernels, absorption, and cohort overlap hold componentwise. Every active selected slice is multiplied by \(1-\varepsilon\), so each order-\(J\) determinant is multiplied by \((1-\varepsilon)^J\neq0\). The four scalar factors cancel in \(K^d\), leaving its simple ordered spectrum unchanged. Hence both laws belong to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\).

Every active slice, \(B_x^{d,\mathcal A}\), \(s_j^d\), and \(\alpha_j^d\) is multiplied by \(1-\varepsilon\), independently of the allocation label. The active transition kernels, spectral signatures, and at-risk effects are unchanged. The all-exit path has \(X_3(1)=X_3(0)=e\), so its causal contrast is zero. Consequently, between the two allocations,
\[
 \nu_j=(1-\varepsilon)\nu_j^\circ,\qquad
 \tau=(1-\varepsilon)\tau^\circ,\qquad
 \eta_j=\eta_j^\circ.                                     \tag{2}
\]
If \(a_j\in\{0,1\}\) indicates that label \(j\) receives the added mass, then
\[
 \pi_j^d=(1-\varepsilon)\pi_j^{\circ,d}+\varepsilon a_j,
 \qquad
 \tau_j=\frac{(1-\varepsilon)\nu_j^\circ}
 {(1-\varepsilon)\pi_j^{\circ,1}+\varepsilon a_j}.       \tag{3}
\]
The denominator is positive because \(\pi_j^{\circ,d}>0\), as derived by \(\texttt{thm:active-frontier-recovery}\). Thus the allocations change the shares of \(h\) and \(k\), and change their full conditional effects whenever the corresponding contribution is nonzero, while all active targets and the aggregate agree.

We next verify the exact specialization from \(\texttt{def:exact-witness}\). Direct row addition gives
\[
 H_j\mathbf1_3=Q_j\mathbf1_3=V_j\mathbf1_3=\mathbf1_3,
 \qquad H_j[e,:]=Q_j[e,:]=V_j[e,:]=(0,0,1).               \tag{4}
\]
All entries are nonnegative. Successive summation of the four-wave mass in \(\texttt{def:exact-witness}\) over \(u_0,u_1,s_2,s_1,s_0,j,d\) gives one. The shared coordinates through date \(2\) prove no anticipation, and setting \(X_t=X_t(D)\) proves consistency. Marginalizing the continuation belonging to the other treatment path gives the first-order Markov factorizations \((H_j,Q_j,Q_j)\) and \((H_j,Q_j,V_j)\). Equation (4) proves absorption. Moreover
\[
 P(D=d)=\frac12,\qquad P(Z=j\mid D=d)=\frac12,             \tag{5}
\]
the latent support is exactly \(\{1,2\}\), and the common untreated kernels at dates \(2\) and \(3\) are \(Q_j\). The active rows of \(H_j\) have zero exit probability, so \(P(X_1=e\mid D=d)=0\).

The predecessor factors are
\[
B_a=\begin{pmatrix}3/16&1/12\\1/16&1/6\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B_b=\begin{pmatrix}1/16&1/6\\3/16&1/12\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det B_a=\frac5{192},\quad\det B_b=-\frac5{192}. \tag{6}
\]
For row \(j\) of \(C_y^0\) use row \(y\) of \(Q_j\), and for row \(j\) of \(C_y^1\) use row \(y\) of \(V_j\). Direct calculation gives the active-minor determinants
\[
 \frac9{50},\quad-\frac3{100},\quad\frac{31}{100},\quad-\frac1{20} \tag{7}
\]
for \((C_a^0,C_b^0,C_a^1,C_b^1)\). Since
\[
 \det M_{xy}^d=\det(B_x)Q_1[x,y]Q_2[x,y]\det(C_y^{d,\mathcal A}), \tag{8}
\]
the determinants ordered as \((aa,ab,ba,bb)\) are
\[
 \left(\frac9{16000},-\frac3{32000},-\frac9{32000},\frac3{12800}\right) \tag{9}
\]
in cohort \(0\), and
\[
 \left(\frac{31}{32000},-\frac1{6400},-\frac{31}{64000},\frac1{2560}\right) \tag{10}
\]
in cohort \(1\). In particular all required anchor-star minors are nonsingular. The cycle diagonal equals
\[
 \operatorname{diag}\left(
 \frac{(3/5)(1/2)}{(1/5)(3/10)},
 \frac{(1/5)(3/5)}{(3/10)(2/5)}\right)=\operatorname{diag}(5,1). \tag{11}
\]
Conjugation by \(B_a\) yields
\[
 K^0=K^1=\begin{pmatrix}29/5&-12/5\\8/5&1/5\end{pmatrix}. \tag{12}
\]
Its trace and determinant are \(6\) and \(5\), so its characteristic polynomial is \((\lambda-5)(\lambda-1)\). Equations (4)--(12) verify every condition defining \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\), as well as no date-\(1\) absorption.

The row vector \((1/2,1/2,0)\) is invariant under both \(H_j\). Hence the treated-cohort type-specific date-\(2\) laws are
\[
 p_{2,1}=(2/5,2/5,1/5),\qquad p_{2,2}=(1/4,1/2,1/4).      \tag{13}
\]
The potential paths share \(X_2\), so iterated expectation under the constructed coupling gives the causal, rather than definitional, identity \(\tau_j=p_{2,j}(V_j-Q_j)\). Direct multiplication yields
\[
 p_{2,1}(V_1-Q_1)=(1/25,0,-1/25),\qquad
 p_{2,2}(V_2-Q_2)=(-1/40,-1/40,1/20).                    \tag{14}
\]
The equal type masses in (5) give
\[
 \tau=(3/400,-1/80,1/200),\quad
 \nu_1=(1/50,0,-1/50),\quad
 \nu_2=(-1/80,-1/80,1/40),                               \tag{15}
\]
and absence of date-\(1\) absorption gives \(\alpha_j^d=1/2\) and \(\eta_j=\tau_j\).

Finally apply (1)--(3) with \(\varepsilon=1/5\), \(h=1\), \(k=2\), and the values in (14). The common active masses are \((4/5)(1/2)=2/5\). The full shares are therefore \((3/5,2/5)\) and \((2/5,3/5)\). Equations (2)--(3) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_1^A&=(2/75,0,-2/75),&
\tau_2^A&=(-1/40,-1/40,1/20),\\
\tau_1^B&=(1/25,0,-1/25),&
\tau_2^B&=(-1/60,-1/60,1/30),
\end{aligned}                                               \tag{16}
\]
and, in both laws,
\[
 \nu_1=(2/125,0,-2/125),\qquad
 \nu_2=(-1/100,-1/100,1/50),\qquad
 \tau=(3/500,-1/100,1/250).                               \tag{17}
\]
Thus the two complete four-wave observed laws coincide, while the asserted full shares and full conditional effects differ and every active target agrees. This establishes both the generic obstruction and every exact numerical assertion.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\) and \(d\in\{0,1\}\). By \(\texttt{ass:cohort-overlap}\), \(P(D=d)>0\), so all conditional probabilities below are defined. For \(x,y\in\mathcal A\), the factors from \(\texttt{def:observed-slices}\) have dimensions
\[
B_x^{d,\mathcal A}\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times J},\quad
D_{xy}\in\mathbb R_+^{J\times J},\quad
C_y^d\in\mathbb R_+^{J\times(m+1)},
\]
and row stochasticity gives \(C_y^d\mathbf1_{m+1}=\mathbf1_J\). By \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\) and \(\texttt{ass:no-anticipation}\), the observed coordinates through date \(2\) equal the corresponding coordinates of either potential path. Conditional first-order Markov factorization from \(\texttt{ass:markov-paths}\), together with \(\texttt{ass:common-date-two-transition}\), therefore gives, for \(u,x,y\in\mathcal A\) and \(v\in\mathcal S\),
\[
 A_{xy}^d[u,v]
 =\sum_{j=1}^J B_x^{d,\mathcal A}[u,j]Q_j[x,y]C_y^d[j,v],
 \qquad
 A_{xy}^d=B_x^{d,\mathcal A}D_{xy}C_y^d.                 \tag{1}
\]
Selecting rows \(\mathcal U\) and columns \(\mathcal V\) yields
\[
 M_{xy}^d=B_x^{d,\mathcal U}D_{xy}C_y^{d,\mathcal V}.    \tag{2}
\]

Every factor in (2) is square of order \(J\). By \(\texttt{ass:four-slice-rank}\), \(M_{x_0y}^d\) is nonsingular for each \(y\in\mathcal A\). The determinant identity in (2) then implies that \(B_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U}\), every \(D_{x_0y}\), and every \(C_y^{d,\mathcal V}\) are nonsingular. The same assumption makes \(M_{xy_0}^d\) nonsingular for each \(x\in\mathcal A\), so every \(B_x^{d,\mathcal U}\) and every \(D_{xy_0}\) is nonsingular. Since transition probabilities are nonnegative,
\[
 Q_j[x_0,y]>0,\qquad Q_j[x,y_0]>0                       \tag{3}
\]
for all \(j,x,y\). In particular, every division below is supported by (3). No inverse of \(M_{x_1y_1}^d\) is used.

Substitute (2) into the four-anchor product defining \(K^d\). The inverses exist by the two arms of \(\texttt{ass:four-slice-rank}\), and cancellation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
K^d
&=B_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U}D_{x_0y_0}C_{y_0}^{d,\mathcal V}
 (B_{x_1}^{d,\mathcal U}D_{x_1y_0}C_{y_0}^{d,\mathcal V})^{-1}\\
&\quad\cdot B_{x_1}^{d,\mathcal U}D_{x_1y_1}C_{y_1}^{d,\mathcal V}
 (B_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U}D_{x_0y_1}C_{y_1}^{d,\mathcal V})^{-1}\\
&=B_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U}\operatorname{diag}_{j}
 \left\{\frac{Q_j[x_0,y_0]Q_j[x_1,y_1]}
 {Q_j[x_1,y_0]Q_j[x_0,y_1]}\right\}(B_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U})^{-1}.
\end{aligned}                                                            \tag{4}
\]
Thus the displayed cross-ratios are the real eigenvalues \(\rho_j^d\). They are distinct by \(\texttt{ass:simple-cycle-spectrum}\). If \(E_j\) is the diagonal matrix with only its \(j\)-th diagonal entry equal to one, polynomial functional calculus applied directly to (4) gives
\[
 P_j^d=\prod_{k\ne j}\frac{K^d-\rho_k^dI_J}{\rho_j^d-\rho_k^d}
 =B_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U}E_j(B_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U})^{-1}. \tag{5}
\]

By \(\texttt{ass:absorbing-exit}\), \(X_0=e\) implies \(X_1=e\). Consequently, on \(X_1=x_0\), the predecessor belongs to \(\mathcal A\), and
\[
 m_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U}=B_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U}\mathbf1_J.
\]
Combining this identity with (5) fixes the eigenvector scale and sign:
\[
 P_j^dm_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U}=B_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U}[:,j]. \tag{6}
\]
Thus the first matrix constructed by \(\texttt{def:recovery-map}\) is the true \(B_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U}\).

Using (1), (3), and (6), for each \(y\in\mathcal A\),
\[
 F_y^d=D_{x_0y}C_y^d,\qquad
 q_{x_0y}^d=F_y^d\mathbf1_{m+1}=D_{x_0y}\mathbf1_J.      \tag{7}
\]
Every coordinate of \(q_{x_0y}^d\) is positive by (3), and hence
\[
 \operatorname{diag}(q_{x_0y}^d)^{-1}F_y^d=C_y^d.        \tag{8}
\]
The selected minor \(C_{y_0}^{d,\mathcal V}\) is nonsingular, so \(C_{y_0}^d\) has row rank \(J\). Therefore
\[
 C_{y_0}^d(C_{y_0}^d)^\top\text{ is invertible},
 \qquad C_{y_0}^d(C_{y_0}^d)^\top
 \{C_{y_0}^d(C_{y_0}^d)^\top\}^{-1}=I_J.                \tag{9}
\]
Equations (1), (8), and (9) imply, for every \(x\in\mathcal A\),
\[
 W_x^d=B_x^{d,\mathcal U}D_{xy_0}.                        \tag{10}
\]
This matrix is nonsingular. Again absorption gives \(m_x^{d,\mathcal U}=B_x^{d,\mathcal U}\mathbf1_J\), so
\[
 c_x^d=(D_{xy_0})^{-1}\mathbf1_J>0,\qquad
 W_x^d\operatorname{diag}(c_x^d)=B_x^{d,\mathcal U}.     \tag{11}
\]
For \(J<m\), the selected rows alone do not determine all predecessor masses. The \(\mathcal A\)-by-\(\mathcal V\) restriction of (1), together with (8) and (11), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_{xy_0}^{d,\mathcal A,\mathcal V}(C_{y_0}^{d,\mathcal V})^{-1}
 \operatorname{diag}(c_x^d)
&=B_x^{d,\mathcal A}D_{xy_0}\operatorname{diag}(c_x^d)\\
&=B_x^{d,\mathcal A}.
\end{aligned}                                               \tag{12}
\]
Thus every predecessor row is recovered. For arbitrary \(x,y\in\mathcal A\), equations (1), (8), and (11) now imply
\[
 q_{xy}^d=(B_x^{d,\mathcal U})^{-1}A_{xy}^{d,\mathcal U,\mathcal S}
 \mathbf1_{m+1}=D_{xy}\mathbf1_J.                       \tag{13}
\]
It follows that \(q_{xy}^d[j]=Q_j[x,y]\), including possibly zero non-anchor transitions. Row stochasticity then identifies
\[
 Q_j[x,e]=1-\sum_{y\in\mathcal A}Q_j[x,y],               \tag{14}
\]
and \(\texttt{ass:absorbing-exit}\) fixes the exit row. Equation (8) identifies every active row of the factual first-post matrix \(R_j^d\), and absorption fixes its exit row as well.

Summing the recovered predecessor probabilities yields
\[
 s_j^d[x]=\mathbf1_m^\top B_x^{d,\mathcal A}[:,j]
 =P(Z=j,X_1=x\mid D=d),
 \qquad \alpha_j^d=\sum_{x\in\mathcal A}s_j^d[x].       \tag{15}
\]
The nonnegative square matrix \(B_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U}\) is nonsingular, so each column is nonzero and has strictly positive column sum. Hence
\[
 \alpha_j^d\geq\mathbf1_J^\top B_{x_0}^{d,\mathcal U}[:,j]>0,
 \qquad
 \pi_j^d=\alpha_j^d+P(Z=j,X_1=e\mid D=d)\geq\alpha_j^d>0. \tag{16}
\]
Thus type overlap is derived from observable anchor-star nonsingularity.

Equations (1) and (8)--(15) recover the complete unnormalized component law on \(\{X_1\in\mathcal A\}\). Explicitly, for \(u,x,y\in\mathcal A\) and \(v\in\mathcal S\), its cell mass conditional on \(D=d\) is
\[
 B_x^{d,\mathcal A}[u,j]Q_j[x,y]R_j^d[y,v],              \tag{17}
\]
while for \(y=e\) it is \(B_x^{d,\mathcal A}[u,j]Q_j[x,e]\mathbf1\{v=e\}\). In particular,
\[
 P(X_2\in\cdot\mid D=d,Z=j,X_1\in\mathcal A)
 =\frac{s_j^dQ_j}{\alpha_j^d}.                            \tag{18}
\]

The ratios in (4) depend only on the cohort-common \(Q_j\), so their strict descending order agrees across cohorts. By consistency, \(R_j^0=U_j\) on active rows. No anticipation makes the treated cohort's \(X_2\) identical under both potential paths, while \(\texttt{ass:common-first-post-untreated-transition}\) makes its untreated continuation kernel equal to \(U_j=R_j^0\). Iterated expectation using (18) proves the causal identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
\nu_j
&=E[\mathbf1\{Z=j\}\{\operatorname{onehot}(X_3(1))-\operatorname{onehot}(X_3(0))\}\mid D=1]\\
&=s_j^1Q_j(R_j^1-R_j^0).
\end{aligned}                                               \tag{19}
\]
This is an equality between the causal target and the recovered observed-law functional, not a definition. If \(X_1=e\) in the treated cohort, consistency gives \(X_1(1)=e\), no anticipation gives \(X_1(0)=e\), and absorption along both potential paths gives \(X_3(0)=X_3(1)=e\). Such units contribute zero to (19). By (16), division is legitimate and
\[
 \eta_j=\frac{\nu_j}{\alpha_j^1}.                         \tag{20}
\]
Finite additivity over the known support \(Z\in\{1,\ldots,J\}\) gives
\[
 \tau=\sum_{j=1}^J\nu_j.                                 \tag{21}
\]
Equations (19)--(21) are exactly \(\Phi(p)=\theta_J\). Every operation uses only the observed law and the declared nonzero margins; therefore the derivation applies to every \(\widetilde P\in\mathcal F(p)\). This proves fiberwise recovery. Only the four matrices in (4) determine the spectral basis, while (8)--(13) use the \(2m-1\) distinct anchor-star slices to transport it to all \(m\) active states. All inputs are marginals of \((D,X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3)\). Thus only four waves are required, and any observed fifth wave may be marginalized out before applying the map.

Let \(q_d(p)=\sum_{s:D(s)=d}p_s\). By \(\texttt{ass:cohort-overlap}\), \(q_d(p)>0\), and every entry of \(A_{xy}^d\) and \(m_x^d\) is a linear marginal of the \(N_m\)-cell four-wave vector \(p\), divided by \(q_d(p)\). The proof of \(\texttt{thm:active-frontier-recovery}\) shows that every inverse and division in \(\Phi\) has a nonzero denominator at a regular compatible law.

To justify the only spectral step, fix one simple eigenvalue \(\rho_j\) of \(K\), right and left eigenvectors \(v_j,w_j\) normalized by \(w_j^\top v_j=1\), and the normalization equation \(w_j^\top v=1\). The derivative with respect to \((v,\rho)\) of \((Kv-\rho v,w_j^\top v-1)\) at \((K,v_j,\rho_j)\) is
\[
 (z,a)\longmapsto((K-\rho_jI_J)z-av_j,w_j^\top z).       \tag{1}
\]
If (1) is zero, left multiplication by \(w_j^\top\) gives \(a=0\); simplicity then gives \(z\in\operatorname{span}(v_j)\), and the last coordinate gives \(z=0\). Thus (1) is invertible. The finite-dimensional analytic implicit-function theorem applied to the polynomial eigen-equations gives a real-analytic local eigenvalue and eigenvector branch. Hence the projector, equivalently the polynomial expression
\[
 P_j=\prod_{k\ne j}\frac{K-\rho_kI_J}{\rho_j-\rho_k},    \tag{2}
\]
is real analytic wherever the spectrum remains simple. Finitely many positive pairwise gaps and the fixed descending order give one common neighborhood. Matrix inversion is rational, and
\[
 C^\dagger=C^\top(CC^\top)^{-1}                          \tag{3}
\]
is analytic wherever \(C\) has full row rank. Therefore the finite composition in \(\texttt{def:recovery-map}\) is real analytic on a relative open neighborhood in the affine hyperplane \(\mathbf1^\top p=1\).

Its Jacobian is directly computable. For a tangent direction \(h\) satisfying \(\mathbf1^\top h=0\), dots denote directional derivatives. Cohort conditioning gives
\[
 \dot q_d=\sum_{s:D(s)=d}h_s,\qquad
 \frac{d}{d\epsilon}\left.\frac{p_s+\epsilon h_s}{q_d(p+\epsilon h)}\right|_{\epsilon=0}
 =\frac{h_s}{q_d}-\frac{p_s\dot q_d}{q_d^2}.             \tag{4}
\]
For every invertible matrix, \(\dot M^{-1}=-M^{-1}\dot M M^{-1}\); the product rule differentiates \(K^d\). For its simple spectral system,
\[
 \dot\rho_j=\operatorname{tr}(P_j\dot K),
 \qquad
 \dot P_j=\sum_{k\ne j}
 \frac{P_k\dot K P_j+P_j\dot K P_k}{\rho_j-\rho_k}.     \tag{5}
\]
Differentiating the recovery formulas yields
\[
 \dot B_{x_0}^{\mathcal U}[:,j]=\dot P_jm_{x_0}^{\mathcal U}+P_j\dot m_{x_0}^{\mathcal U},
 \quad
 \dot F_y=-B_{x_0}^{-1}\dot B_{x_0}F_y+B_{x_0}^{-1}\dot A_{x_0y},
 \quad \dot q_{x_0y}=\dot F_y\mathbf1_{m+1},             \tag{6}
\]
\[
 \dot C_y[j,:]=\{\dot F_y[j,:]-\dot q_{x_0y}[j]C_y[j,:]\}/q_{x_0y}[j]. \tag{7}
\]
Writing \(N=(C_{y_0}C_{y_0}^\top)^{-1}\),
\[
 \dot C_{y_0}^\dagger=\dot C_{y_0}^\top N-C_{y_0}^\top N
 (\dot C_{y_0}C_{y_0}^\top+C_{y_0}\dot C_{y_0}^\top)N,  \tag{8}
\]
and therefore
\[
 \dot W_x=\dot A_{xy_0}C_{y_0}^\dagger+A_{xy_0}\dot C_{y_0}^\dagger,
 \quad \dot c_x=W_x^{-1}(\dot m_x-\dot W_xc_x),          \tag{9}
\]
\[
 \dot B_x^{\mathcal U}=\dot W_x\operatorname{diag}(c_x)+W_x\operatorname{diag}(\dot c_x). \tag{10}
\]
The product rule applied to \(B_x^{\mathcal A}=A_{xy_0}^{\mathcal A,\mathcal V}(C_{y_0}^{\mathcal V})^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(c_x)\), and then to the recovered \(Q_j,R_j^d,s_j^d\), gives their derivatives. Finally,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\dot\nu_j
&=\dot s_j^1Q_j(R_j^1-R_j^0)+s_j^1\dot Q_j(R_j^1-R_j^0)\\
&\quad+s_j^1Q_j(\dot R_j^1-\dot R_j^0),
\qquad \dot\tau=\sum_{j=1}^J\dot\nu_j.
\end{aligned}                                               \tag{11}
\]
Equations (4)--(11) determine \(J_\Phi(p)h\), including the derivative of every active mass.

Let \(\mathcal S_0\) be the actual finite support stratum and suppose \(p_s>0\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S_0\). Saturated scores are exactly the functions \(a\) with \(E_Pa(O)=0\), because \(p_{\epsilon,s}=p_s\{1+\epsilon a(s)\}\) remains a probability vector for sufficiently small \(|\epsilon|\). Along this path,
\[
 \left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\Phi(p_\epsilon)\right|_0
 =J_\Phi(p)\sum_sp_se_sa(s)
 =E_P\{J_\Phi(p)(e_O-p)a(O)\}=E_P\{G_p(O)a(O)\}.        \tag{12}
\]
Also \(E_PG_p(O)=0\). Since the saturated tangent space is all of \(L_2^0(P)\), (12) identifies \(G_p\) as the canonical gradient. Its covariance is
\[
 E_P[G_p(O)G_p(O)^\top]
 =J_\Phi(p)\{\operatorname{diag}(p)-pp^\top\}J_\Phi(p)^\top=\Sigma(p). \tag{13}
\]
If a centered influence vector \(H\) represents the derivative of a regular asymptotically linear estimator, then (12) gives \(E_P\{(H-G_p)a\}=0\) for every \(a\in L_2^0(P)\). Taking each coordinate of \(H-G_p\) as a score proves \(H=G_p\) almost surely. Thus (13) is the saturated information bound.

Finally, \(\texttt{ass:iid-panels}\) gives the exact empirical identity
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat p-p)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n(e_{O_i}-p).   \tag{14}
\]
Taylor expansion of the analytic map gives
\[
 \sqrt n\{\Phi(\widehat p)-\Phi(p)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nG_p(O_i)+o_P(1).                   \tag{15}
\]
The summands have finite support and are bounded. Thus, for every fixed vector \(u\), their centered characteristic function satisfies
\[
 E_P\exp\{iu^\top G_p(O)/\sqrt n\}
 =1-\frac{u^\top\Sigma(p)u}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}).
\]
Taking the \(n\)-th power proves convergence of the linear term in (15) to \(N(0,\Sigma(p))\), allowing a singular covariance. The same expansion under a differentiable local multinomial path \(p_n=p+n^{-1/2}\dot p+o(n^{-1/2})\), together with Taylor's formula, gives the deterministic shift \(J_\Phi(p)\dot p\); hence the plug-in is regular on the stratum. Therefore the empirical four-wave plug-in has canonical influence function \(G_p\) and attains the saturated finite-multinomial bound. No efficiency assertion is made for the smaller restricted Markov observed-law image.

Let \(\mathcal K_\kappa\) be the set of \(N_m\)-cell four-wave vectors induced by \(\mathcal P_\kappa\). It is compact by \(\texttt{def:buffered-class}\). The finite margin vector contains every inverse, division, pairwise eigengap, normalization, and label margin used by \(\Phi\), and \(\texttt{ass:variance-buffer}\) covers every reported diagonal. Population margins are at least \(2\kappa\), whereas the empirical guard uses \(\kappa\).

Analyticity, continuity of the finite margin list, and compactness give \(r>0\) such that the relative closed \(r\)-neighborhood of \(\mathcal K_\kappa\) lies in the analytic domain and passes every algebraic and variance guard at level \(\kappa\). On this neighborhood,
\[
 L_1=\sup_q\|J_\Phi(q)\|<\infty,
 \qquad L_2=\sup_q\|D^2\Phi(q)\|<\infty.                \tag{1}
\]
Absorption-legal support holds almost surely under each class member. By \(\texttt{ass:iid-panels}\), direct multinomial calculation gives
\[
 E_P\|\widehat p-p\|_2^2=\frac{1-\|p\|_2^2}{n}\leq\frac1n,
\]
and hence
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\kappa}P(\|\widehat p-p\|_2>r)
 \leq\frac1{nr^2}.                                        \tag{2}
\]
This proves uniform guard acceptance, including the buffered variance check.

Taylor's formula on the event in (2) gives
\[
 \left\|\sqrt n\{\Phi(\widehat p)-\Phi(p)-J_\Phi(p)(\widehat p-p)\}\right\|
 \leq\frac{L_2}{2}\sqrt n\|\widehat p-p\|_2^2.          \tag{3}
\]
The probability that the right-hand side exceeds \(\epsilon>0\) is at most \(L_2/(2\epsilon\sqrt n)\), uniformly in \(P\). Combining (3), the exact empirical identity, and \(\Phi(p)=\theta_J\) from \(\texttt{thm:active-frontier-recovery}\) proves the uniform linear representation.

The empirical covariance has the exact finite-multinomial form
\[
 \widehat\Sigma=J_\Phi(\widehat p)
 \{\operatorname{diag}(\widehat p)-\widehat p\widehat p^\top\}
 J_\Phi(\widehat p)^\top.                                 \tag{4}
\]
The right-hand side is uniformly continuous on the compact neighborhood, so (2) proves uniform covariance consistency. In particular, every reported empirical diagonal exceeds \(\kappa\) with probability tending to one uniformly. No covariance inverse is used.

It remains to establish coverage when the limiting correlation is singular. Take an arbitrary sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_\kappa\). Compactness supplies a subsequence for which \(p_n\to p_\star\), and continuity gives \(\Sigma(p_n)\to\Sigma(p_\star)\). For \(\ell\in\mathcal L\), put
\[
 \sigma_{n,\ell}^2=\Sigma_{\ell\ell}(p_n)\geq2\kappa,
 \qquad Y_{n,i,\ell}=G_{p_n,\ell}(O_i)/\sigma_{n,\ell}. \tag{5}
\]
The vectors \(Y_{n,i}\) are centered and uniformly bounded by (1) and the diagonal buffer. After a further subsequence their correlation matrices \(\Gamma_n\) converge to a positive-semidefinite unit-diagonal matrix \(\Gamma_\star\), which may be singular. For fixed \(u\), a third-order Taylor expansion with uniformly bounded remainder gives
\[
 E_{P_n}e^{iu^\top Y_{n,1}/\sqrt n}
 =1-\frac{u^\top\Gamma_nu}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}).              \tag{6}
\]
Independence then makes the characteristic function of \(n^{-1/2}\sum_iY_{n,i}\) converge to \(\exp(-u^\top\Gamma_\star u/2)\). Hence the studentized linear term converges to \(Z_\star\sim N(0,\Gamma_\star)\), including when \(\Gamma_\star\) is singular.

Conditionally on the sample, the multiplier numerator is exactly Gaussian and its studentized correlation is
\[
 \widehat\Gamma_{\ell k}=\frac{\widehat\Sigma_{\ell k}}
 {\sqrt{\widehat\Sigma_{\ell\ell}\widehat\Sigma_{kk}}}. \tag{7}
\]
Covariance consistency and the positive reported diagonal imply \(\widehat\Gamma\to\Gamma_\star\) in \(P_n\)-probability. The already established \(\texttt{lem:gaussian-max-quantile-continuity}\) applies to positive-semidefinite unit-diagonal matrices, including singular limits. Therefore
\[
 \widehat c_{1-\alpha}\to c_\star,
 \qquad
 P\left(\max_{\ell\in\mathcal L}|Z_{\star,\ell}|\leq c_\star\right)=1-\alpha. \tag{8}
\]
Uniform linearization, (4), and the lower variance bound show that replacing the studentized linear term and its population standard deviations by the plug-in quantities changes the maximum by \(o_{P_n}(1)\). The limit distribution in (8) is continuous, so the joint coverage probability along the selected subsequence converges to \(1-\alpha\).

If uniform convergence failed, there would be a sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_\kappa\) whose coverage stayed a fixed positive distance from \(1-\alpha\). The preceding compactness argument would give a subsequence, and then a further subsequence, along which coverage converges to \(1-\alpha\), a contradiction. Thus coverage converges uniformly and, in particular, the displayed infimum tends to \(1-\alpha\). The proof requires only positive reported marginal variances; neither \(\Sigma(p)\) nor its correlation matrix need be nonsingular.

\[

\]
Consequently the residual is nonzero exactly when the last display is positive, equivalently when \(g_a\notin\operatorname{col}(W^{-1}A)\). This closes the projection calculation conditional on a valid full-stratum chart, but construction and rank certification of that chart remain open.

prose_updates.tldr: For fixed known \(2\leq J\leq m\), four observed waves \(X_0,\ldots,X_3\) suffice. Four anchor slices determine the spectral basis, and \(2m-1\) fixed selected anchor-star minors transport it to every active state despite a common absorbing boundary. Projectors, stochastic row sums, a full-row-rank pseudoinverse, and full-predecessor-row transport recover active component sublaws, type contributions, at-risk effects, and the aggregate first-post ATT on the broad class; no date-\(1\) absorption upgrades these to full type shares and full conditional type effects. The resulting \(N_m=2\sum_{r=0}^{4}m^r\)-cell functional has an explicit saturated multinomial canonical gradient and guarded uniform Gaussian-multiplier bands under singular correlation. Restricted-model efficiency remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published short-panel Markov-mixture reconstruction and the closest transition-independence theorem impose rank, positivity, homogeneity, emission, or state-count conditions that do not deliver four-wave causal recovery at a common absorbing boundary. They also do not characterize the initial-absorber frontier, where full latent shares and conditional type effects can fail although active contributions and the aggregate remain identified.
project_justification.niche: For fixed known \(J\leq m\), fixed ex ante row and column selections, and an observable anchor star of \(2m-1\) nonsingular selected minors, four anchor slices identify a common spectral basis while the remaining star slices transport it across active states. Stochastic normalization handles exit, and absorption plus no anticipation makes date-\(1\) absorbers a zero-effect component.
project_justification.fill: The paper gives the explicit four-wave known-\(J\) projector, row-sum, pseudoinverse, and full-row transport map; proves the active-versus-full target frontier and a generic initial-absorber allocation counterexample; verifies an exact rational \(J=m=2\) witness; and derives the analytic saturated gradient plus guarded uniform multiplier bands.

sampling_model.design: Observational two-cohort four-wave panel \(O=(D,X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3)\), with adoption at date \(3\), a finite active state space of size \(m\), a common absorbing exit, fixed known \(2\leq J\leq m\), and possible date-\(1\) absorption in the headline class.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent and identically distributed complete four-wave panels on the \(N_m=2\sum_{r=0}^{4}m^r\)-cell absorption-legal support; \(N_2=62\). A recorded fifth wave is unnecessary and may be marginalized out.
sampling_model.treatment: Cohort membership fixes the realized path; no anticipation holds through date \(2\), and units absorbed by date \(1\) have identical absorbed potential continuations through the first post-treatment date.
sampling_model.overlap: Both cohorts have positive probability. Positive active masses \(\alpha_j^d\) and hence positive full masses \(\pi_j^d\) follow from anchor-star nonsingularity rather than a separate type-overlap assumption.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance is fitted. Empirical frequencies on the fixed four-wave \(N_m\)-cell support feed the guarded analytic anchor-star recovery map.

prose_updates.related_work: Ahn and Kasahara (2026), Proposition 14 and Appendix A.4, provide the closest inverse-cancellation architecture, but their stated full-rank and positive-transition conditions exclude the common absorbing boundary; the present four-wave result is an excluded-boundary extension, not an application of their theorem. Higgins and Jochmans (2023) and Gupta, Kumar, and Vassilvitskii (2016) reconstruct Markov mixtures under their own homogeneity, component-rank, state-count, and nondegeneracy regimes; their scaling and label ideas are prior art, whereas the present theorem is causal, time-varying, and uses fixed known \(J\leq m\) selected anchor-star minors. Restricted hidden-Markov reconstruction results impose emission or other structural restrictions and do not prove the potential-path contribution identity here. Deaner and Ku (2026) study aggregate duration difference-in-differences rather than latent-type multi-state reconstruction. Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2017) motivate differentiating diagonalization estimators, while Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, 2015) are neighboring Gaussian-bootstrap and anti-concentration references. Rao and Risch (2026) are an interpretation consumer only: this paper does not claim their data satisfy the latent Markov, rank, support, or iid conditions. Restricted-model efficiency is left as an explicit open question.
prose_updates.interpretation:
The four-wave result separates the full type share \(\pi_j^d\), active share \(\alpha_j^d\), unnormalized contribution \(
u_j\), and at-risk effect \(\eta_j\). The \(2m-1\) anchor-star slices identify \(\alpha_j^d\), \(
u_j\), and \(\eta_j=
u_j/\alpha_j^1\), with positivity derived from nonsingularity. They cannot allocate already-absorbed zero-effect mass across latent labels, so full shares and full conditional effects need not be identified. If date-\(1\) absorption is absent, \(\pi_j^d=\alpha_j^d\) and \(	au_j=\eta_j\). The exact \(H_1,H_2,Q_1,Q_2,V_1,V_2\) witness verifies the cycle operator, type effects, and aggregate rationally, while its all-exit reallocation exhibits the frontier. Rao and Risch's incumbent-firm setting motivates this decomposition but is not reanalyzed.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The covariance \(\Sigma(p)\) is the canonical-gradient bound for the declared off-model continuation \(\Phi\) in the saturated four-wave finite-multinomial support-stratum model. The paper does not parameterize the smaller restricted Markov observed-law image, certify its score Jacobian on constant-rank strata, or claim its efficiency bound or an attaining estimator. The exact multiplier quantile is the mathematical object; a fixed Monte Carlo draw count requires separate approximation analysis. Weak eigengaps, changing selected-minor rank, unknown \(J\), adaptive anchor selection, clustered sampling, and approximate common kernels remain outside the result.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper proves a sufficient constructive frontier for fixed finite \(m\), known \(2\leq J\leq m\), four observed waves, fixed ex ante selected sets and anchor pairs, \(2m-1\) observable anchor-star nonsingularity conditions, distinct common cycle signatures, cohort overlap, type-conditional first-order Markov potential paths through date \(3\), no anticipation, absorption, and common untreated date-\(2\) and first-post kernels. It derives rather than assumes type positivity. The exact rational witness establishes nonvacuity and the initial-absorber pair establishes the stated obstruction. The paper does not identify unknown type count, choose minors adaptively, cover weak or complex spectra, justify dependent-panel inference, or solve restricted-model efficiency. Full conditional type effects require no date-\(1\) absorption; the broad class identifies active sublaws, contributions, at-risk effects, and the aggregate.

statement_notes.justification: The four-wave generic allocation family certifies the sharp initial-absorber obstruction, while the rational \(J=m=2\) coupling verifies nonvacuity and every displayed normalization exactly.
statement_notes.gap: Absorbing-outcome DiD and generic mixture results do not isolate a four-wave reallocation of initial zero-effect absorbers that changes full conditional effects while preserving all active targets.
statement_notes.consumer: Researchers can use date-1 exit as a falsifiable support diagnostic and avoid interpreting full conditional latent-type effects when initial absorbers are present.

statement_notes.justification: This is the field-level four-wave identification theorem: it transports a four-anchor spectral basis over all active states for fixed known \(J\leq m\), derives type positivity, and proves the aggregate-versus-full-conditional frontier.
statement_notes.gap: Adjacent reconstruction theorems do not combine a common absorbing boundary, \(2m-1\) selected anchor-star minors, four-wave time-varying causal paths, and the initial-absorber effect decomposition.
statement_notes.consumer: An analyst may marginalize any fifth wave and report latent-type contributions and the aggregate when the four-wave anchor-star guard passes, even if full latent allocation of already-exited units is unavailable.

statement_notes.justification: Analyticity makes the fixed-known-J four-wave recovery algorithm an explicit regular finite-multinomial estimator and exposes its saturated canonical gradient on each actual support stratum.
statement_notes.gap: Prior diagonalization asymptotics do not give the canonical gradient of this four-wave absorbing-boundary anchor-star, row-sum, pseudoinverse, and full-row transport map.
statement_notes.consumer: The four-wave delta-method covariance propagates estimated active masses and transported predecessor factors without introducing unidentified full shares.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem combines the buffered four-wave empirical guard with singular-correlation Gaussian-max quantile continuity for uniform simultaneous inference.
statement_notes.gap: Gaussian anti-concentration alone does not establish guard acceptance and uniform Taylor control for the rational four-wave recovery map.
statement_notes.consumer: Users can jointly report all J contribution vectors and their aggregate from four-wave panels despite structural covariance singularity.

statement_notes.justification: This remains an explicit four-wave open question: restricted efficiency requires a full observed-law chart, a certified constant-rank score Jacobian, and a projection calculation.
statement_notes.gap: Only the saturated four-wave multinomial canonical gradient is established; the restricted Markov score space is not characterized.
statement_notes.consumer: Future work must construct the chart and evaluate the residual projection before claiming a sharper restricted-model bound or attainment.
